payload.verdict: A mathematics teacher moving into analytics, with useful projects that need to lead the story.
write_up: Your resume tells the story of a mathematics teacher at Cedar Ridge and Eastside Preparatory moving into data analytics. A recruiter can see your teaching work and your tools, but the analytics projects arrive after the teaching jobs, and the housing analysis doesn't say what you found. I read this first as a Mathematics Teacher resume with an analytics transition underway.

The Student Performance Dashboard is your best model: it names the Excel dashboard, the measures and the time period, then says the math department used it to choose units for re-teaching. Your summary names the move into analytics but not the job you want, while the projects that demonstrate that move sit below your experience.

Let's bring the data projects closer to the top and name the analytics role you're targeting. Then add the housing analysis finding and make the Cedar Ridge assessment work more concrete. Those changes will help a recruiter connect your teaching experience to the work you want next.

cards.line: Passionate about using data to tell stories and drive decisions. Strong analytical, communication, and problem-solving skills with a proven track record of success.
cards.cannot_tell: These claims don't show a recruiter what you analyzed or which decision used your work. Your student dashboard gives you a concrete example to put here instead.
cards.example: Mathematics Teacher transitioning into data analytics; built an Excel dashboard tracking AP Statistics pass rates and quiz scores over three years, used by the math department to decide which units needed re-teaching.
cards.question: Which analytics role do you want this summary to point toward?

cards.line: The summary names data analytics but not a target job, and Data Projects sits below Professional Experience.
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter sees the teaching jobs before the projects that show your analytics work. Name the job you're seeking and consider moving the projects above your experience for that application.
cards.question: Which analytics job are you targeting, and which project is most relevant to it?

cards.line: Developed and implemented engaging curriculum aligned with state standards
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter knows the curriculum aligned with state standards, but not what you developed or changed. One concrete piece of the work would distinguish it from a general teaching duty.
cards.example: Developed and implemented [curriculum component] aligned with state standards.
cards.question: What did you develop or change in the curriculum?

cards.line: Analyzed student assessment data to identify learning gaps and adjust instruction
cards.cannot_tell: This connects analysis to instruction, which is useful for your transition. The missing piece is what the assessments showed and how you adjusted the teaching.
cards.example: Analyzed student assessment data to identify [learning gap] and adjusted instruction by [instructional change].
cards.question: What learning gap did you find, and how did you adjust instruction?

cards.line: Served as Math Department Data Lead, compiling benchmark results for department meetings
cards.cannot_tell: The data lead work belongs in your analytics story. A recruiter can't tell what the benchmark results measured or what you brought to the meetings.
cards.example: Served as Math Department Data Lead, compiling benchmark results on [measures] for department meetings.
cards.question: What did the benchmark results you compiled measure?

cards.line: Communicated regularly with parents and administrators regarding student progress
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can see who you communicated with, but not what information you shared about progress. Name the work behind those conversations.
cards.example: Communicated regularly with parents and administrators regarding [student progress information].
cards.question: What information about student progress did you share?

cards.cannot_tell: Participation doesn't say what you contributed or worked on with the group. Give the recruiter one part of that work to hold onto.
cards.example: Participated in professional learning communities focused on [work or topic].
cards.question: What did you work on in the professional learning communities?

cards.line: Analyzed 10 years of Austin housing and income data using Python and SQL
cards.cannot_tell: The tools and time period are clear, but the finding is missing. A recruiter looking for analytics work will want to know what the housing and income data showed.
cards.example: Analyzed 10 years of Austin housing and income data using Python and SQL, finding [finding].
cards.question: What did your analysis find?

cards.line: Built an Excel dashboard tracking AP Statistics pass rates and quiz scores over three years
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as a model. It names what you built and what it tracked; the next line adds the department's use of it.

fit.why: Your two dated roles are mathematics teaching jobs, and your recent work includes assessment analysis and a department data lead assignment.
fit.level: mid-level, Mathematics Teacher and Math Department Data Lead
fit.note: Your teaching experience gives you a strong subject-matter foundation, while the bootcamp and dashboards show an entry-level path into analytics. Put the most relevant project near the top when applying for an analytics role.
